Treatment summary
Patient presented following a side-impact collision at an intersection with complaints of neck pain and stiffness.
Imaging was not required at initial evaluation. Over the course of 18 visits, care consisted of manual therapy, targeted
stretching, and a home exercise program. The mechanism of injury and the forces involved are consistent with the
cervical strain diagnosed. Range of motion was reduced on initial examination, and palpable paraspinal muscle
tenderness was documented, while neurological screening and strength testing remained within normal limits
throughout. Reoprted symptoms followed an expected recovery pattern, with visit frequency decreasing as pain and
mobility improved. No prior complaints or treatment involving the cervical region are known to this provider. Billing
records reflect single charges for each service rendered, with no duplicate or repeated billing identified. Prognosis is
good with continued self-directed exercise, and discharge from active care is anticipated.
</page>
